findings.title: format() rounds negative half values toward zero, asymmetric with positives (and yields '-1 seconds')
findings.property_test: format sign symmetry at half boundaries
findings.actual: '-1s'; long form gives '-1 seconds' (plural suffix chosen from |ms| >= 1.5*unit, but number rounded by Math.round to -1)
findings.evidence: Math.round(-1.5) === -1 whereas Math.round(1.5) === 2; the plural() helper uses msAbs for pluralization, so it intends symmetric handling of negatives, yet yields ungrammatical '-1 seconds' vs '2 seconds' for the positive.

error.message:
Expected values to be strictly equal:

'-1s' !== '-2s'

review.title: format() rounds negative half-unit values toward +infinity, giving '-1 seconds' for -1500 ms
review.reason: In src/index.ts, fmtShort and plural() decide the unit and the plural suffix from msAbs, but round the signed value with Math.round(ms / n). For -1500 the suffix logic treats the value as 1.5 or more and adds 's', while Math.round(-1.5) gives -1, so the output is '-1 seconds' (and '-1s'), where 1500 gives '2 seconds' ('2s'). Existing tests cover negatives only at non-half values, so nothing contradicts a fix. The fix is tiny (round the absolute value and reapply the sign). The impact is cosmetic and limited to exact .5 boundaries, so a maintainer might defer it.
